record.summary: Establishes consumer protections for AI companions. Operators must disclose that users are interacting with AI, provide crisis resources, adopt response protocols for user prompts about suicidal ideation or self-harm and report annually to the Behavioral Health Administration of the Department of Health. The Act sets guidelines against addictive software patterns aimed at minors and against chatbots presenting themselves as human; AI companions may not pose as licensed mental health professionals or encourage harmful behaviour, and violations are subject to Hawaii's consumer protection laws.
record.notes: SB 3001, 'Relating to Artificial Intelligence', was signed by Governor Josh Green on 14 July 2026 as Act 248, at a bill-signing ceremony on AI together with HB 2137 (Act 247), which provides civil remedies against unauthorized AI-generated realistic digital imitations of individuals. Senator Jarrett Keohokalole co-introduced the bill. The Governor's release of 15 July 2026 closing the 2026 bill-signing period lists it among the 266 of 267 measures of the 2026 session that became law.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Office of the Governor of Hawaii news release of 15 Jul 2026 ('Gov. Green Completes Bill Signing Season and Issues Veto Decision', governor.hawaii.gov, stored 12 Oct 2026) and the Transparency Coalition's tracker article (transparencycoalition.ai, not an official site; stored again on 17 Oct 2026 with only a byline change). The 15 Jul release confirms that SB 3001 became Act 248 and describes its content. Stored in this run: the Governor's release of 14 Jul 2026 ('Gov. Green Signs Legislation to Support Kupuna Care and Strengthen AI Protection', governor.hawaii.gov/?p=12919), which says the Governor 'today signed' three measures including SB 3001, Act 248, and describes its disclosures, response protocols, annual reports and protections for minors; it supports date_published from an official source. Governor's Message No. 1350 (data.capitol.hawaii.gov), which would carry the Act text and its effective-date section, was requested but could not be stored. The 14 Jul 2026 effective date therefore rests only on the tracker, and the Act's own text has not been read; the summary follows the two Governor's releases.
